The National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities has funded the Community CATALYST Center ([P20MD019799](https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/10977025)), led by [OCHIN](https://ochin.org) with Rachel Gold, Karen Albright, and Hossein Estiri as principal investigators.

GridEX is the environmental data behind the center. OCHIN supports community health centers across the country on a shared electronic health record. Linking GridEX to that record lets the center study how extreme temperature events relate to health care use and outcomes in safety-net populations, at the 500 m resolution where exposure actually differs between neighborhoods.

The linkage is also a test of what GridEX was built for: a gridded exposure resource that joins to health data regardless of the geographic units those data use.

Read more about [GridEX](../gridex.qmd) or [download the data](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/DJGKDJ).
